query: Starting from a W–Cu composite containing W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix, what single intervention could overcome phase separation and interfacial void formation, thereby improving thermal conductivity relative to the untreated composite under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions relevant to joints between W-based plasma-facing materials and Cu-based cooling components? Formulate one hypothesis that states the intervention, the proposed mechanism, the predicted comparative outcome, the applicable processing and service boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a high-temperature solid-state diffusion bonding process to the W–Cu composite, specifically at temperatures near but below the melting point of Cu, will reduce phase separation and interfacial void formation, resulting in improved thermal conductivity under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions relevant to W/Cu joints.
generation.material_initial_state: W–Cu composite containing W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix, with typical phase separation and interfacial voids.
generation.intervention: High-temperature solid-state diffusion bonding at temperatures just below Cu melting point (e.g., 1000–1080°C), under moderate pressure and inert atmosphere.
generation.conditions: Processing: 1000–1080°C, moderate pressure, inert atmosphere. Service: Heat-transfer and irradiation conditions relevant to plasma-facing material joints.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced interfacial bonding and reduced voids at W–Cu interfaces due to atomic diffusion and improved wetting.
generation.mechanism: Diffusion bonding promotes atomic intermixing and eliminates interfacial voids, reducing phase separation and improving thermal contact between W and Cu phases, thereby increasing effective thermal conductivity.
generation.predicted_outcome: Thermal conductivity of the treated composite will be measurably higher than that of the untreated composite under relevant heat-transfer and irradiation conditions.
generation.baseline: Untreated W–Cu composite with typical phase separation and interfacial voids.
generation.boundary: Applicable to W–Cu composites with sufficient initial interfacial contact; limited by thermal stability of Cu and absence of excessive grain growth or melting.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of thermal conductivity improvement depends on initial microstructure and bonding parameters; lack of direct evidence for irradiation stability post-bonding.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of W–Cu composites: one untreated, one subjected to high-temperature diffusion bonding. Subject both to heat-transfer and irradiation tests simulating plasma-facing joint conditions. Measure thermal conductivity and inspect for interfacial voids and phase separation.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the diffusion-bonded composite does not show reduced voids, improved interfacial bonding, or higher thermal conductivity compared to the untreated composite under relevant conditions, the hypothesis is falsified.
